function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: We need to log foods. The user says they had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We should log each item. For each log_food call, we need to provide food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We can assume default meal_type snack? But maybe we can specify meal_type based on context: mango likely snack, chai tea maybe breakfast? But user didn't specify times. We could default to snack. Provide log_date? Could use current timestamp? But we don't have actual date/time. We can leave log_date null. So we need to make calls to log_food for each item: 8 pieces of frozen mango (food_name: "frozen mango"? portion_amount: 8, portion_unit: "piece"), meal_type: snack. Then chai tea: food_name: "chai tea", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup" maybe? Or "piece"? Tea is usually cup. So portion_unit: "cup". Then pepperoni pizza: food_name: "pepperoni pizza", portion_amount: 2, portion_unit: "slice". Coffee: food_name: "coffee", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup". We'll call log_food four times.
